_intro: The words in these prompts that carry the technique rather than the subject. These are the parts you can lift out and paste into a prompt about something else. Each term recurs across several subjects and categories, and the precision notes show how to phrase the most context-sensitive ones.
_rule: A term is in this file only if it appears in at least 3 entries across at least 2 categories. Below that it is subject vocabulary, not transferable vocabulary. build_vocabulary.py enforces the rule and refuses to build if a term stops meeting it.

groups.framing: where the camera is and how the frame is cut
groups.light: what the light does, and where it comes from
groups.surface: how the material reads up close

terms.n: Pulls in to subject-fills-frame distance. The most reliable single word in this catalog for changing scale.
Wide. Expect converging verticals and a stretched foreground.
Reportage width. Keeps the surroundings in the story.
Roughly what the eye does. The neutral choice.
Compresses and separates. Portrait glass.
Background goes soft and reads as photography. For a drawn or painted style, use simplified background detail instead.
terms.finding: It changes medium willingly and scene content reluctantly

terms.n: Same idea, phrased as a result rather than a setting.
Flattens distance and stacks the background against the subject.
Moving things smear, still things stay sharp. Water and cloud respond most.
Camera above the subject looking down, not necessarily square to it.
Asks for a true plan view. Pair it with a flat subject, symmetrical layout, and no visible horizon.
terms.finding: "Straight down" is a request, not an instruction

terms.n: A concise way to request an overhead plan view. Add flat lay or no visible horizon when the angle matters.
Objects arranged on a plane, seen from above. More reliable than asking for the angle directly.
Camera below eye level. Makes the subject loom.
Turned partly away. The default product and portrait angle.
Tight on the subject without the optical character of macro.
Mirrors the composition about a centre line. Holds well.
Subject on the axis. Useful when a layout keeps drifting.
Parallel projection, no vanishing point. Reliable enough to be its own category here.
Parts separated along their assembly axes.
Section removed to show the inside.
Light skimming across a surface at a shallow angle. The single best phrase in this catalog for making texture visible.
Soft, sourceless, no hard shadow. Names what the light does rather than what makes it.
Flat and shadowless. What you want when the subject is the thing, not the mood.
The shorter form.
Frontal, minimal modelling.
Sharp-edged shadows, small source.
From one side. Modelling and shadow across the form.
Says there is an axis without naming a fixture.
Source behind the subject. Edges glow, front goes dark.
Colour temperature as an instruction. Note that a colour word in a black-and-white prompt will fight it.
Direction and temperature together.
Creates soft directional daylight and may include the window. Use broad side light when you want only the effect.
terms.finding: Name a light and you get the light. Name the softbox and you get the softbox.

terms.n: Creates cool, even overhead light. Mention ceiling tubes only when they belong in the composition.
terms.finding: Name a light and you get the light. Name the softbox and you get the softbox.

terms.n: Creates a strong warm cast with an indoor evening feel.
One source. Constrains the shadow story.
Used to place the origin explicitly.
Implies a low source without naming one.
Large source, diffuse edge.
Subject dark against a bright field. Removes surface detail on purpose.
No specular highlight.
Specular, reflective. Brings the surroundings into the surface.
Film grain, wood grain or screenprint grain depending on the noun it sits next to. All three work.
Exposure damage, fading, oxidisation.
Use damage: rubbed edges, thinned paint, softened corners.
Aged metal specifically.
Diffusing, translucent rather than transparent.
Creates a repeat-inspired surface motif. Use a tiling post-process when you need production-ready edges.
terms.finding: "Seamless" produces a pattern that does not tile

terms.n: Impression into the paper, ink sitting in the debossed area.
Cut line, most reliable on metal and stone.
Prussian blue, white line work.
Opaque water paint, visible brush loading.
Transparent washes, paper showing through.
Spot colour, misregistration, visible screen.
Pulls saturation down across the frame.
The same, stated as a constraint on the whole palette.
Restricts the palette. Name the exact hues for the clearest visual direction.
terms.finding: It counts objects. It does not count attributes.

terms.n: The general handle. Almost always worth naming explicitly.
Stronger than muted.
Builds the image around one hue. Add grayscale or black-and-white when that is the intended treatment.
terms.finding: A negative clause costs you almost nothing, and I said the opposite

terms.n: Widens the tonal range, crushes the middle.
A named neutral. Neutrals drift unless you say which way.
